findings.basis: correctness / input contract (item.rules[3], the diagnostic's own advice)
findings.failure_scenario: state.json holds a started step with an unknown key (for example `mystery.1`, written by a newer conductor or injected). `resume` stops with STAGE_RECOVERY_UNKNOWN and its message tells the owner to 'settle the item or retry it'. Neither works. `settle` (run_service.py:262-275) only sets outcome, stop and partial and leaves steps alone. `reconcile_interrupted` walks every item whatever its outcome, so the next `resume` stops again on the same key. `resume --retry W1` cannot help either: `_reconcile_interrupted()` runs at run_service.py:73, before the `for ref in retry` loop at :75, and `retry` also requires outcome == blocked, which an item interrupted mid-step does not have. The run can then never be resumed again without editing state.json by hand, which the contract places outside its rules.
findings.reproduction: Static reading (my reproduction script was blocked by the sandbox): opened_run({'mystery.1': {'status': 'started'}}); resume -> STAGE_RECOVERY_UNKNOWN; settle(run, 'W1', 'done', 'x'); resume -> STAGE_RECOVERY_UNKNOWN again; resume(retry=('W1',)) -> STAGE_RECOVERY_UNKNOWN before retry is reached.

triage_reproduction.cmd: read packages/orch/lib/orch/conductor/application/run_service.py:64-86 and recovery.py:37-67 (static; a runtime run was not possible in the sandbox)
triage_reproduction.observed: resume calls _reconcile_interrupted() at line 73 before the retry loop at line 75; reconcile_interrupted iterates all items regardless of outcome and raises Stop STAGE_RECOVERY_UNKNOWN on an unknown started key; settle (lines 262-275) does not modify steps. So neither settle nor --retry can clear the key.

findings.failure_scenario: With checks.overlap_review, `checks.N` is marked started outside `step()`. If the review raises a Stop other than REVIEW_CANCELLED (for example a provider or budget stop) while the background checks have raised (`computed.exception()` is not None), `_run_checks` is skipped and the Stop propagates. `checks.N` stays `started`, not `stopped`. The next resume then emits STAGE_INTERRUPTED 'repeated' (or 'repeated after tree change' plus CHECK_CHANGED_TREE) for a run that ended with an ordinary Stop, not a crash. That breaks item.rules[2], which requires a stop to be recorded as stopped and resumed without STAGE_INTERRUPTED.

triage_reproduction.observed: _start_step marks checks.N started at line 144; when the review raises a non-REVIEW_CANCELLED Stop and computed.exception() is not None, no _run_checks call happens and `raise` leaves checks.N in status started instead of stopped.

findings.failure_scenario: Two problems in the executor note. (a) Outside git, `base_head` is null, so the note says 'since None: ...'. (b) With a clean tree it says 'since <sha>: . Continue ...', an empty list. The executor gets a prompt that names a non-existent base or no paths. Rule 4 fixes the template text, but how null and empty values are rendered is up to the implementation.
